10.1d — 3-Button Jam: Friend Playtest & Triage

You have stared at your own scene for three days, so your brain already fills in every missing hint and unfair hitbox automatically. Today you rotate stations so three friends playtest your 3-Button game cold — and you practice the hardest skill in software: watching silently without explaining anything while someone breaks what you made.

Protocol: How to Run a Friend Playtest (~10 min prep) ~10 min
  1. Before standing up: make sure your scene displays your 3 button keys right on screen (or on a tiny folded index card beside the keyboard) so you never have to explain them verbally.
  2. The Silence Rule: press Play, step back half a chair, and DO NOT touch the mouse or speak while your tester plays for 90 seconds. If they ask "Wait, does J do anything right now?" answer kindly with "Keep trying what looks right" and write down that question!
  3. Watch eyes + fingers, not just the screen: watch which keys their fingers hunt for, when they lean forward, when they look bored, and the exact moment they lose without understanding why.
Three Rotations: Gather Evidence (~35 min) ~35 min

Swap seats with three different friends (about 10 minutes per pair: 3 min play + 2 min debrief each way):

Friend #First 10 Seconds (Did They Get the 3 Buttons?)Biggest Friction / Confusion MomentExact Bug or Balance Surprise
Friend 1
Friend 2
Friend 3

Good debrief questions to ask AFTER they finish:

  • "Which of the three buttons felt unnecessary or confusing?"
  • "Tell me what you thought killed you on your fastest loss."
  • "Did the game get harder in a way that felt exciting or random?"
Triage: Rank Revisions Before Coding (~15 min) ~15 min

Do not try to implement every suggestion a friend throws out ("add a shop! add multiplayer!"). Sort every observation into priority buckets so your next work session makes the biggest leap:

  • P0 — Broken / Unplayable: crashes, soft-locks, impossible starts, restart failures, buttons unresponsive.
  • P1 — Clarity & Core Friction: player could not tell what hurt them, forgot what Button 3 does, difficulty ramped unfairly fast, hitboxes felt deceptive.
  • P2 — Feel & Polish: audio feedback, color flashes, animation smoothing, particles.

Socratic: Reading Playtest Data Honestly

  1. Name ONE surprise that happened to two or all three friends — why did it catch them off guard when it seemed completely obvious to you?
  2. Write down one polite friend suggestion you are intentionally choosing to IGNORE (say why it misses your core 3-button focus or blows your jam scope).
  3. State your concrete Revision Contract for next class: list your top P0/P1 fix, the exact script or scene change it requires, and how you will prove the revision worked.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Observe three classmates play your build silently and log concrete facts for each run
  • Gather debrief answers without arguing with or defending your design
  • Prioritize findings cleanly into P0 (broken), P1 (clarity/balance), and P2 (polish)
  • Lock in a clear Revision Contract before touching code next class
